1Introduction

Angkor Wheels Rental is the management system behind a motorbike rental business based in Siem Reap, Cambodia. It has two connected parts:

  • A public website where customers browse the available motorbikes, check pricing, and submit a rental request online.
  • An admin panel where staff manage the fleet, review and confirm bookings, track customers, record payments, and monitor the business.

This guide documents the admin panel in detail, since that is where staff spend most of their time, and also covers the customer-facing website so admins understand what customers see.

Who should use this guide

  • Business owners and managers who need the full picture of what the system can do.
  • Front-desk / rental staff who create walk-in bookings, confirm payments, and hand out motorbikes.
  • Anyone new to the team who needs to learn the system quickly.

Main benefits

  • One place to see every booking, whether it came from the website or a walk-in customer.
  • Automatic conflict checking, so the same motorbike can never be double-booked for overlapping dates.
  • A 50% deposit rule enforced consistently for every booking, online or in person.
  • Support for Cambodia-specific payment methods — KHQR, ABA, ACLEDA, Wing, and card — alongside cash for walk-ins.
  • Built-in reporting on revenue, bookings, fleet utilization, and customers.
  • A bilingual public website (English and Khmer) so both local and international customers can book comfortably.

2System Requirements

Angkor Wheels Rental is a web application — there is nothing to install. It runs in a standard internet browser on a computer, tablet, or phone.

RequirementDetails
Supported browsersGoogle Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox, or Safari (recent versions of any of these).
Screen sizeThe admin panel is designed for a laptop or desktop screen (1280px wide or larger) for the most comfortable experience. It remains usable on a tablet.
Internet connectionA working internet connection is required at all times — the system stores all data on a central server, not on your device.
AccountAn admin account (email + password) created by a Super Admin. See Section 13 for the roles available.
ℹ
The public booking website is fully responsive and works well on customers’ phones, which is how most rental inquiries happen in practice.

3Login

All staff access the system through the admin login page.

  1. Open the admin login page in your browser.
  2. Enter your email address.
  3. Enter your password.
  4. Click Log In.

Forgot your password?

Click "Forgot password?" on the login screen and enter your email address. If an account exists for that address, a password reset link is sent to it, valid for one hour.

Incorrect login

If the email or password is wrong, the system shows an error message and does not log you in. Contact a Super Admin if you keep being rejected — they can check whether your account is still active from the Users page (Section 13).

4Dashboard

The Dashboard is the first page you see after logging in. It gives a quick, at-a-glance summary of how the business is doing today.

What is on the dashboard

  • A personalized greeting with today’s date and two shortcut buttons: New Booking and Add Motorbike.
  • Fleet Overview cards — Total Motorbikes, Available, Currently Rented, and In Maintenance.
  • Bookings & Revenue cards — Pending Bookings, Today’s Revenue, This Week, and This Month.
  • A Revenue by Month chart and a Bookings by Month chart, both covering the last 12 months.
  • A Booking Status Breakdown chart showing the proportion of bookings that are pending, confirmed, active, completed, or cancelled.
  • A Top Performing Motorbikes list, ranked by revenue, with the two top spots marked with gold/silver rank badges.

Every number on the dashboard is live — it reflects the current state of the database, not a cached snapshot.

5Navigation

The left-hand sidebar is how you move between every part of the admin panel. It is organized into three groups.

GroupMenu itemsPurpose
Rental ManagementMotorbikes, Reservations, Bookings (List), Customers, Maintenance, ReportsEverything to do with running day-to-day rentals.

The sidebar can be collapsed to a narrow icon-only strip using the arrow button at the top, to give more room to the page content.

The top bar

Every admin page has a top bar showing a breadcrumb trail (e.g. "Admin / Bookings"), the page title, a light/dark mode toggle, and your account menu on the right.

6Managing Motorbikes

Purpose: The Motorbikes section is where the entire rental fleet is recorded — one entry per physical motorbike, with its specifications, pricing, photos, and current status.

Fields on a motorbike

FieldDescriptionRequired
NameThe display name shown to customers, e.g. "Honda Click".Yes
Brand / ModelThe manufacturer and model, e.g. Honda / Click 125i.Yes
Engine CCEngine size in cubic centimeters.Yes
Transmission / Fuel TypeAutomatic, Manual, or Semi-Automatic; Gasoline or Electric.No (has a default)
Plate Province / Plate CodeThe Cambodian province printed on the plate (selected from a list of all 25 provinces, or the national plate) and the plate code, e.g. ភ្នំពេញ 1AC-2345.No
Key TypeNormal Key or Smart Key.No
Daily / Weekly / Monthly PriceRental rates. Weekly and monthly rates are optional discounted tiers.Daily price is required
Deposit / Delivery FeeThe refundable security deposit and any hotel-delivery fee.No
Min / Max Rental DaysThe shortest and longest booking length allowed for this bike (a half-day booking of 12 hours or less always bypasses this).No
StatusAvailable, Rented, Maintenance, or Inactive.Yes

Adding a motorbike

  1. Click Add Motorbike from the Motorbikes list (or the dashboard shortcut).
  2. Fill in the Basic Information, Rental Information, and Features sections.
  3. Click Create Motorbike.
  4. On the next screen, upload photos — the first photo, or the one marked as primary, is what customers see first.

Editing a motorbike

Open the motorbike from the list and click the pencil (Edit) icon, or click into any row. All fields can be changed, including photos, on the same screen.

Deleting / deactivating a motorbike

Use the trash icon to permanently delete a motorbike, or the toggle icon to mark it Inactive without deleting it (useful for a bike that is temporarily out of service, e.g. sold or being repaired long-term — see also Section 9, Maintenance, for shorter repairs).

⚠
Deleting a motorbike is permanent and requires the Admin or Super Admin role. Staff accounts cannot delete motorbikes or bookings.

Searching and filtering

Use the search box to find a motorbike by name, brand, model, or plate number/province, and the status dropdown to show only Available, Rented, Maintenance, or Inactive bikes.

7Reservations & Bookings

Purpose: this is the heart of the system — every rental, whether submitted by a customer on the website or created by staff for a walk-in, is a booking.

The Reservations calendar

The Reservations page opens in Calendar view by default, with KPI cards at the top (Today’s Reservations, Active Rentals, Returning Today, Available Motors, Upcoming This Week, Pending Approval, and Unpaid/Partial).

Each day on the calendar shows how many bookings fall on it, with a colored dot for each status (pending, confirmed, active rental, returned, cancelled). Click any day to see the full list of bookings for that day.

Switch to Table view using the toggle in the top-right for a traditional sortable, filterable list instead of a calendar.

Creating a new booking (walk-in / staff-created)

  1. Click New Booking from the Reservations page, the Bookings list, or the dashboard shortcut.
  2. Choose the motorbike and the pickup/return date and time — the estimated total and required 50% deposit are calculated automatically.
  3. Choose an existing customer by searching their name or phone, or switch to "New" and enter a new customer’s details.
  4. Set the Booking Status (Pending, Confirmed, Active, or Completed) and the payment details — Payment Status, Paid Amount, and Payment Method.
  5. Click Create Booking.
ℹ
Walk-in customers are usually recorded as Confirmed right away, since they are physically present. Bookings from the public website start as Pending until a staff member reviews and confirms them.
⚠
Any booking status other than Pending or Cancelled requires at least 50% of the total to be marked as paid. The form shows a warning and blocks saving if the amount is not enough.

The Bookings list

Bookings (List) shows every booking as a sortable table with search and status filtering.

Booking detail page

Opening a booking shows the full customer, rental, and financial details, an editable "Adjust Booking" form, a "Return & Deposit" section, a status-update panel, and a timeline of every status change.

Updating a booking’s status

Use the Update Status panel on the right side of the booking detail page: choose the new status, optionally add a note, and click Update Status.

When a booking is marked Returned, the system automatically records the return time and suggests a late fee if it is configured (see Section 12, Settings) and the bike came back after its scheduled return time. The late fee and any deposit refund amount remain editable in the "Return & Deposit" section.

Deleting a booking

Open the booking and click Delete Booking at the bottom of the Adjust Booking form. A confirmation dialog appears before anything is removed.

⚠
Deleting a booking is permanent and requires the Admin or Super Admin role.

8Customers

Purpose: every person who has ever booked a motorbike — through the website or as a walk-in — has a customer record, automatically created the first time they book (matched by phone number) and reused for every later booking.

Customer information

FieldDescriptionRequired
Full NameThe customer’s name.Yes
PhoneUsed to match repeat customers automatically.Yes
Email, Nationality, Telegram, WhatsAppOptional contact details.No
ID Type / ID or Passport NumberID Card or Passport.No
ID Document PhotoAn uploaded photo of the ID/passport, if provided at booking time.No

Opening a customer shows their profile plus their full booking history in one place.

Customer details can be edited directly from their profile page. Staff, Admin, and Super Admin accounts can all edit customer information.

9Maintenance

Purpose: track service history for each motorbike — oil changes, tires, brakes, engine work, battery, general service, and accident repairs.

Each maintenance record captures the motorbike, the type of work, a date, optional odometer reading, cost, garage name, and a status of Scheduled, In Progress, or Completed.

ℹ
Maintenance records are separate from a motorbike’s overall Status field. Setting a motorbike’s status to "Maintenance" hides it from customer bookings while it is being worked on; the Maintenance section keeps the detailed repair history regardless of that status.

11Reports & Export

Purpose: the Reports page turns the raw booking and customer data into business-level numbers, for a date range you choose.

Selecting a date range

Use the quick buttons (Today, Last 7 days, Last 30 days, This month, This year) or pick exact From/To dates, then click Apply.

What the report shows

  • Revenue & Financials — total revenue, subtotal, discounts given, and extra charges, plus a revenue-over-time chart and a breakdown by payment status (Unpaid / Partial / Paid).
  • Bookings & Rentals — total bookings, average rental length, cancellation rate, amount paid to date, and a breakdown by booking status.
  • Motorbike Performance — a table of every motorbike with its bookings, revenue, utilization percentage, and maintenance cost for the period.
  • Customers — new vs. returning customers, a ranked list of top customers by spend, and a breakdown by nationality.

Exporting data

Three CSV export buttons are available at the top of the page: Bookings / Revenue, Motorbikes, and Customers. Clicking one downloads a CSV file for the currently selected date range, which opens directly in Excel or Google Sheets.

ℹ
CSV is currently the only export format. There is no PDF export or print-formatted report inside the application; the CSV file can be opened and printed from a spreadsheet program if a printed copy is needed. There is also no data import feature — all records are entered through the forms described in this guide.

12Settings (Content & Policies)

Purpose: control everything about how the public website looks and behaves, organized into tabs.

TabWhat it controls
Business InfoBusiness name, currency, phone, email, address, description, footer text, and whether email notifications are sent (see below).
Social MediaTelegram, WhatsApp, Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok links shown on the site.
HomepageThe hero title, subtitle, and background image on the homepage.
AboutThe About page’s title, description, story, mission, and image.
Payment MethodsLive KHQR account details (for an automatically generated QR code with the exact amount), plus instructions shown to customers for ABA, ACLEDA, Wing, and Card payments.
Rental PolicyMinimum age, min/max rental days, required documents, and the policy text shown on the public Rental Policy page (deposit, fuel, late return, damage, cancellation, accident, traffic violation, and helmet policies), plus the late-fee-per-hour rate.

Every tab is saved with the same Save Settings button; changes apply to the public website immediately.

Email notifications

When enabled, the system automatically emails a confirmation to the customer when a booking is created, a status-update email whenever the booking’s status changes, and an alert to the business email address for every new booking. Sending email requires an SMTP mail server to be configured by whoever manages the server — if none is configured, these emails are simply skipped rather than causing an error.

13Website Content: Banners, FAQ, Locations, Messages

These four menu items, under the Website group, manage smaller pieces of public website content.

Banners

Promotional banners shown on the site, each with a title, subtitle, image, an optional button, an active/inactive toggle, a display order, and an optional start/end date for time-limited promotions.

FAQ

Question-and-answer pairs shown on the public FAQ page, with a display order and an active/inactive toggle.

Locations

Pickup/return locations offered to customers, each with an address, description, Google Maps link, phone number, and opening/closing hours.

Messages

Messages submitted through the public Contact page arrive here. Each can be marked as read/unread so the team can track which inquiries still need a reply.

14User Roles & Permissions

Purpose: the Users page (Settings group) manages who can log in to the admin panel and what they are allowed to do. Only a Super Admin can access this page.

The three roles

RoleDescription
Super AdminFull access to everything, including creating other admin/staff accounts and changing roles.
AdminFull access to running the business — motorbikes, bookings, customers, settings, reports — except managing user accounts.
StaffDay-to-day front-desk work: create and edit bookings, edit customer details, manage maintenance records, and view everything else. Cannot add/edit/delete motorbikes, change settings, delete bookings, or manage users.

Permission matrix

ActionSuper AdminAdminStaff
View dashboard, bookings, motorbikes, customers, reportsYesYesYes
Create / edit bookingsYesYesYes
Delete bookingsYesYesNo
Edit customer detailsYesYesYes
Create maintenance recordsYesYesYes
Add / edit / delete motorbikesYesYesNo
Change settings, banners, FAQ, locationsYesYesNo
Manage admin/staff usersYesNoNo

Creating a user

  1. Go to Settings → Users.
  2. Fill in the new user’s full name, email, and a password (minimum 8 characters).
  3. Choose their role — Staff, Admin, or Super Admin.
  4. Click Create User.

An existing user’s role can be changed at any time from the dropdown next to their name, and their account can be deactivated (blocking login without deleting their history) using the Deactivate button.

15Profile / Account

Your account menu, in the top-right of every admin page, shows your name and role.

From here you can:

  • See your current role (Super Admin, Admin, or Staff).
  • Log out of the admin panel.
ℹ
There is currently no self-service "edit my profile" or "change my password while logged in" page. To change a password, use "Forgot password?" on the login screen (Section 3) to receive a reset link by email. A Super Admin can also update your name, email, or role from the Users page.

16Common Errors & Troubleshooting

ProblemPossible CauseSolution
Cannot log inIncorrect email or password, or the account has been deactivatedDouble-check your email and password. If it still fails, ask a Super Admin to confirm your account is active.
"At least $X (50%) must be paid" when saving a bookingThe booking is being set to a status other than Pending/Cancelled without enough of the deposit recordedIncrease the Paid Amount to at least 50% of the total, or leave the status as Pending until payment is confirmed.
"Motorbike is already reserved..." errorThe chosen motorbike already has an overlapping booking for those datesPick different dates, choose a different motorbike, or check the Reservations calendar for that bike’s availability.
A motorbike doesn’t appear for customers to bookIts status is set to Maintenance or InactiveOpen the motorbike and change its status to Available once it is ready to rent again.
No data shows in a listA search term or filter is still applied from a previous visitClear the search box and reset any status/date filters.
Booking confirmation emails are not arrivingNo SMTP mail server has been configured, or email notifications are turned offAsk whoever manages the server to configure SMTP settings, and check that "Send email notifications" is enabled under Settings → Business Info.
Can’t delete a motorbike or bookingYour account role is StaffAsk an Admin or Super Admin to perform the deletion.

17Frequently Asked Questions

Can a customer book directly from the website?

Yes. Customers browse motorbikes, choose dates, enter their details, choose a payment method, and submit the request. It arrives in the admin panel as a Pending booking for staff to review and confirm.

Does the system accept real online payments automatically?

Payments are not processed automatically by a payment gateway. For KHQR, the system generates a real, ready-to-scan QR code with the exact amount filled in. For ABA, ACLEDA, Wing, and Card, the customer is shown payment instructions and can upload a screenshot as proof; staff then confirm the payment manually in the booking.

What happens if a customer returns the motorbike late?

If a late-fee-per-hour rate is configured (Settings → Rental Policy), the system automatically suggests a late fee when the booking is marked Returned, based on how many hours late it was. Staff can adjust this amount before saving.

Can the same motorbike be booked twice for overlapping dates?

No. The system checks for date overlaps every time a booking is created or edited, for both website and staff-created bookings, and blocks the save with an error if there is a conflict.

Is the public website available in Khmer?

Yes. Customers can switch between English and Khmer using the language switcher in the site header. The admin panel itself is English-only.

Can I get a printed copy of a report?

Export the report as a CSV file and open/print it from Excel or Google Sheets — there is no built-in "print report" button inside the application.
